entries.hook: The new Apple CEO's first move was a folding phone. Bold, or a mistake?
entries.pain: You don't want to drop a grand on the wrong one — or ruin your pocket line with a phone that doesn't fold flat under a tailored jacket.
entries.solution: My real verdict on all three, tested against how they actually carry — so you buy the one that fits your life, not just the keynote.

entries.hook: The wildest tech story of the decade just became a movie you can't look away from.
entries.pain: You half-remember the OpenAI boardroom chaos from the headlines, and you don't want to be the guy at dinner who doesn't get the reference.
entries.solution: My breakdown of what's true, what's dramatized, and why it's the first AI-era movie actually worth watching twice.

entries.hook: Sixteen years after The Social Network, Sorkin's back — and nobody walks out of this one looking cool.
entries.pain: You loved the first film but you're not sure a sequel-in-spirit can hit as hard without feeling like a lecture.
entries.solution: My read on why this one's sharper and darker — and exactly why I'm more excited to watch Strong get cross-examined than Eisenberg get famous.

entries.hook: Some men walk into any room like they own it. That's not confidence — it's something else entirely.
entries.pain: You've felt like an outsider in a room that mattered — a boardroom, a gallery, a members' bar — and wondered if that feeling ever actually goes away.
entries.solution: The sociology behind it, plus my own story of building a second one — so the next room doesn't need translation.

entries.hook: Two houses. Two one-off Porsches. Neither one a compromise between them.
entries.pain: Most 'collab cars' are just a logo slapped on someone else's engineering — a gimmick dressed up as a collectible.
entries.solution: Inside both builds — what LV and Singer actually each brought — and why this is the rare pairing that earns the price tag.

entries.short_title: You Live It Before You Sell It
entries.hook: I'm building the biggest men's lifestyle brand the world has ever seen. Here's the confession behind it.
entries.pain: You've watched brand founders talk a big game while the substance behind it feels thin — and wondered if that's just how it has to be.
entries.solution: My own boardroom story — why the brand was never going to be the proof. I was.

entries.hook: No hour markers. No subdial. No face at all. So how do you actually read the time?
entries.pain: You want a watch that says something different, but most 'no-dial' pieces feel like a gimmick you can't really wear or read.
entries.solution: Why Berneron let the mechanism BE the dial — and exactly what that costs you in legibility versus what it gives you in presence.

entries.hook: Guy Ritchie's title is a joke with a straight face — and almost nobody catches it.
entries.pain: You watched The Gentlemen for the plot twists and missed the actual thesis about who really wins a room.
entries.solution: Reading the film through Pierre Bourdieu's sociology — so your next rewatch, you see exactly what Ritchie was really saying.
